variant_RISE_standard.blur_rule: blur is directional (y >> x) and tracks velocity: sigma_y ~= velocity_px_per_frame / sqrt(12) (box blur one full frame of travel = 360-degree shutter motion blur). Implement as motion blur, or as filter blur on y only.

line_stagger.rule: line 2 uses the SAME tween as line 1, offset by N frames; N measured = 1 (A), 2 (B), 0 (D), 7 (E), 5 (F), 2 (G), 14 (H), 2 (I). Median 2 f. N is NOT constant; long delays (H, E) look speech-paced (H: line 2 lands as "organic" is spoken).
line_stagger.order: top line first, always (also when the top line is the pink one: E, I)
line_stagger.within_line: no per-word or per-letter stagger: every word of a line moves and fades in lockstep (fit residual < 0.04 with one rigid layer per line)

hold.rule: static: zero motion, zero scale drift during hold (C: frame diff 0.0 for 30 f). Only the pink gradient fill keeps animating.

exit.default: hard cut: the text disappears in one frame with no fade/scale/move. Usually the camera cut removes it (C, E, F, G, H, I).
exit.variant_hard_cut_mid_shot: A, B: text cut out mid-shot after exactly 35 visible frames (A 5 f before the camera cut, B 56 f before).

keyframes.camera_cut_relation: Entrance is independent of cuts: first visible frame is 0-2 f after a cut (B +2), or 30-80 f into the shot (A, C, D, E, F), or 2 f BEFORE the cut and continuing across it (G).
keyframes.speech_relation: first visible frame leads the matching spoken word by ~140-300 ms (B "what" +138 ms, G "What" +137 ms, I "AB" +167 ms, D "video" +270 ms; YouTube auto-caption word times, +/-100 ms).

pattern.keyframes: Camera shots alternate A↔B most (A→B 23, B→A 22), with W inserted as the third angle (A↔W 27, W→B 10, B→W 6). Never the same framing twice in a row. Graphics/screencasts are entered from any camera and exit to any camera. Camera shot medians: A 3.7 s, W 3.1 s, B 2.7 s (B close-ups are the shortest); full-screen MG median 7.0 s, SC 8.1 s.

keyframes.result: 85 camera→camera cuts vs YouTube ASR word onsets and 10-ms mid-band energy: cut-frame speech energy is a median 11.8 dB below the local speech level and 61% of cuts sit in a pause (<-10 dB); the next word starts a median 123 ms after the cut (p25 68, p75 197 ms) and the previous word is sentence/clause-final in most cases (e.g. "today.", "framework.", "screen.", "visuals."). → cuts land in the inter-sentence gap, ~0.1-0.2 s BEFORE the next sentence starts.

keyframes.ducking: no evidence of sidechain ducking: in 13 pauses ≥500 ms the bed is −31.1 dB in the first 100 ms and −34.8 dB in the last 100 ms (would rise if ducked). Treat as a constant low bed (~−32 dBFS RMS) under VO, raised only for the outro.

sfx_summary.keyframes: Of 20 graphic/UI events, 9 show a clearly non-voice HF transient (HF−mid ≥ +6 dB, global p90 is −3.4 dB) within −150…+165 ms of the first visible frame; median of those ≈ +60 ms after the visual (bar2 +123, click2 +73, research +90, keep +17, bar3 +145, pinks +50, cpl +100, organic −108, morph −43, runnext −147). Envelopes are short (30-90 ms at −6 dB) → pops/clicks; the two longer ones (runnext 120 ms, e-com 130 ms + 300 ms rise) are whoosh-like and LEAD the visual. Recipe: pop/click SFX with transient at +2 f (≈ +60-120 ms) after the element's first frame; whooshes start ≈ 4-8 f before a word that enters on a cut.

screencast.about: Screencast production SYSTEM (motion + rules, design-free) derived from Jake's own tutorials: reference 2 (kwysV2smgfY) + refs 3–5 (3Jq-L6uLd28, Geg9TyNoi3w, AZxFgIVgHjg, measured 2026-10-07). Explained in aieditor/screencast/SYSTEM.md. camera.py reads ['camera'], agent_rec.mjs reads ['recorder'] (via env), qa.py reads ['qa']. Colours/cursor sprite/marker colour = STYLE in camera.py, not here. 2026-10-07: Jake's 19-point review of v11 (SYSTEM.md §0) overrides earlier rules: subject centre-middle, constant motion (holds ≤ 6 s), bubble fixed (fades only for actions under it), bubble-first transitions to/from full-screen narration, gradient behind every text overlay.

long_prompt_scroll._doc: long_prompt_scroll (MO07) — MEASURED motion from motion6.mov (Claude.ai dark chat view, 1920x1200 capture, app content = y 60-1139 = 1920x1080 1:1, 60 fps, 331 frames = 5.517 s). Frame f (1-based) = t (f-1)/60 s. Camera tracked with ORB + RANSAC similarity per frame (pure zoom about a fixed pivot, then pure vertical translation). The capture repeats ~every 5th frame (≈48 fps source) — fits use unique frames only. Design-free: zoom as a scale about a frame-fraction pivot, scroll in message LINES, sweeps in seconds.

zoom._doc: one zoom-in from the whole app view (scale 1) to `scale` about a fixed pivot (frame fractions; ref pivot 949.9, 452.5 px ±1 px). Ref: start frame 66.43 (t 1.090 s), 38.8 frames (0.647 s; the long ease tail settles by frame ~110), fitted on the unique (non-repeated) capture frames. The first highlight starts sweep_after_zoom_start_s after the zoom starts (ref 1.504 s, i.e. while the zoom is 66 % through). If hl_0 is earlier than zoom + sweep_after_zoom_start_s the zoom moves earlier (never before in + min_start_after_in_s).

scroll._doc: the scroll down the message (ref: ONE move, start frame 192.5 = t 3.192 s, 84 frames = 1.40 s, 966.5 screen px at zoom 1.8959 = 509.8 start-view px = 17.58 message lines (line pitch 29.0 start-view px); mean 12.56 lines/s, peak 27.1 lines/s (1493 screen px/s)). READING-SPEED LIMIT: a move lasts max(min_dur_s, lines / max_lines_per_s) — never faster on average than the reference. A move starts so that the phrase it brings in is fully inside the visible band exactly on its beat (ref: the sweep started 0.054 s after the move started, the phrase entering at the bottom edge), but never before the previous move has ended nor less than min_dwell_after_sweep_s after the previous sweep ended (ref dwell 1.11 s). One move takes as many following phrases as fit between style.layout.top_y and rest_bottom_y (ref: phrases 1-3 in one move). lead_s: a move starts at least this long before the sweep of the phrase it brings in (ref 0.054 s).

sweep._doc: marker highlight: a rounded yellow box grows left→right over each LINE PIECE of the phrase; the text under it is redrawn dark. The reference's sweep is a FIXED-DURATION keyframe (same progress values 0.044/0.156/0.317/0.50/0.683/0.844/0.956 on every sweep, independent of width 90-588 px): dur_s 0.358 (fits 0.333-0.375 s). A wrapped phrase's next line piece starts piece_offset_s after the previous piece STARTS (ref 0.242 s; pieces overlap). A phrase's sweep starts at max(its beat hl_i, previous phrase's last piece start + piece_offset_s, the moment it is fully visible). Ref sweep starts (= the replica's beats): 1.504 / 3.246 / 4.204 / 4.454 s. Highlights accumulate and stay to the end. late_tol_s: a sweep may start up to this much after its beat without a warning.

hold._doc: static hold after the last sweep ends (ref: last sweep end 4.787 s → clip end 5.517 s)

exit._doc: the reference has no exit animation (hard cut); 'out' beat = cut

Times in seconds; 'at' = offset from the beat it hangs off. Travel in card px at the resting scale (card = 1034 px wide).

prompt_highlight._doc: prompt_highlight (MO06) — MEASURED motion from motion5.mov (Claude.ai composer screen-captured from YouTube; content area y 60-1139 of the 1920x1200 capture = 1920x1080, 1:1). Times in seconds. Reference sweep starts (= the hl beats of the replica): 1.959 / 3.703 / 5.449 s; clip 8.617 s. Design-free: travel in units of the prompt font em or of the frame.

push._doc: camera push-in: a pure scale about a fixed pivot (frame fractions), from 1 to `scale`; it ENDS when the first highlight sweep starts (ref: start 1.217 s = frame 74.0, 0.742 s long, first sweep at 1.959 s). Fit by Nelder-Mead on the button/logo centroid distance (scale) — rms 0.0125, max 0.033 of the travel (the source refreshed at ~24 fps).

type._doc: typing: one character at a time at a constant rate (ref 30.6 chars/s across 166 chars, segments 29.7-33.3; the source capture refreshed at ~24 fps so it showed 1-2 new chars per update). The caret is visible while typing and disappears hide_after_s after the last character. If a phrase would not be typed by its beat at the natural rate, the text before it is typed faster (up to max_cps) so it is complete lag_s before the beat.

grow._doc: the composer grows one line height when the text wraps; the growth STARTS lead_s before the first character of the new line appears and lasts dur_s (ref: frames 179.9-202, first char on the new line at frame 201). Greeting stays fixed (top-anchored); the composer grows downward and pushes the suggestion chips down. The text is laid out in full from the start (words never jump lines while typed).

sweep._doc: marker highlight: a rounded yellow box grows left→right over each LINE PIECE of the phrase (piece by piece when the phrase wraps), the text under it turns dark at the edge. Piece duration = clamp(width_em * s_per_em, min_s, max_s) (ref pieces: 15.1 em 0.382 s, 20.8 em 0.497 s, 24.1 em 0.493 s, 5.85 em 0.151 s). Next line piece starts line_gap_s after the previous piece ends. Sweep i starts at max(beat hl_i, phrase typed + after_typed_s, push end, previous sweep end). Highlights accumulate (stay on); they never merge — the word between two highlights ('and') stays unhighlighted to the end (checked frames 300-517).
sweep._ease_note: one ease for every piece (joint fit over sweeps 0/1/2: rms 0.021, max 0.077 — the max is sweep 0, which runs a little slower in the middle right after the push lands)

hold._doc: static hold after the last sweep ends (ref 2.68 s, last sweep end 5.93 s → clip end 8.617 s)

exit._doc: the reference has no exit animation (hard cut); 'out' beat = cut

prompt_menu.units: seconds; px are REFERENCE px at 1080p for the reference layout (composer 1232 px wide) and are multiplied by the layout scale (composer on-screen width / 1232) when the UI or item count changes
prompt_menu._quantize_note: the reference is a 30 fps screen recording doubled to 60 fps: every motion sample is held 2 frames (samples on odd 60 fps frames). null = smooth.

appear._note: menu + composer are fully on screen from the first frame (no entrance in the reference); hard cut on beat 'in'

hover._note: the row highlight AND the composer's placeholder preview switch on the same frame, 0.11 s after the cursor starts the hop (≈ when the tip crosses into the row); no fade

entry._note: t relative to the first hover (row 0 highlight); dx,dy px relative to the cursor's rest point on row 0; alpha = opacity (fade-in while already moving in from the right)

rest._note: where the tip rests on row i: x as a fraction of the menu width from the menu's left edge; y as a fraction of the row pitch from the row's band top (uniform pitch model). Rows beyond 5 reuse rows 2-4 cyclically.

hop._note: hop into row i starts switch_after_hop_start_s before that row's hover beat; fitted linear, max error 1.2 px (cubic in-out fits were 2.9-7.5 px worse)

click._note: no press feedback on the cursor or the row: the pick is shown only by the collapse

send._note: after 'out' the cursor travels to the composer's send button: t relative to beat 'out'; u = per-axis progress from the pick rest point (0) to the end point (1) = send-button centre + end_offset_frac_of_button × button diameter

collapse._note: t relative to beat 'pick' (= the click). The composer text commits (preview grey → solid) at +0; the whole group pans up so the composer re-centres while the menu shrinks about its bottom centre and is removed at +0.145 s

composer_pan._note: travel = 191.5 px in the reference (720 px/s); final composer centre = frame centre + 0.0766 × composer height

menu_opacity._note: no fade: still fully opaque at +0.128 s, gone at +0.161 s

out._note: the reference ends on a hard cut 0.667 s after the cursor starts toward the send button (it has just arrived)
out._note_menu_false: menu:false (composer only): the cursor's measured entry glide lands on the send button on 'out' (the click); the clip holds 0.5 s and cuts

typing._note: motion3 has no typing; the typing for the 'prompt' parameter is the MEASURED typing of motion4 (prompt_card_3d.kf.json typing: 110 chars in 1.55 s, 71 cps, ease, caret solid, gone 0.47 s after the last char). It starts 0.1 s after the collapse pan settles (or on beat 'type'); 'out' waits until 0.3 s after the last char.

tagline_build.source: motion2.mp4 (1920x1080, 60 fps, 92 f; f90-91 are already the NEXT shot) - measured 2026-10-09
tagline_build.units: seconds. U = the text's CAP HEIGHT at scale 1 (reference 92 px @1080). Positions in U relative to the anchor named per table. Rect = text ink box (ink left/right, cap top, baseline) + pad.

words._note: each word pops in fully opaque on its beat (no fade, no blur, no offset) at scale 0.94 about its own ink centre and settles to 1

rect._note: the 4 handles' home rectangle (= the handles' exact positions on the first frame)

dots._note: 11 feeder dots (24 px) travel Manhattan-style legs (axis-aligned run, then a diagonal) into the 4 corner handles and vanish on contact (merge_s); each merge fattens the handle 24 -> 40 px. Tables: [t from word_0, dx_U, dy_U] relative to the feeder's target rect corner. Handles: gather [t from word_0, dx_U, dy_U, d_U] relative to their rect corner (they wander ~0.2 U after the merges = the 'absorbed momentum').

exit._note: progress_table [time fraction, x progress, y progress] = the measured per-frame flight (used by the JS); ease_x/ease_y = fitted summary (no anticipation)
progress_table [time fraction, x progress, y progress] = the measured per-frame flight (used by the JS); ease_x/ease_y = fitted summary (no anticipation)
progress_table [time fraction, x progress, y progress] = the measured per-frame flight (used by the JS); ease_x/ease_y = fitted summary (no anticipation)
progress_table [time fraction, x progress, y progress] = the measured per-frame flight (used by the JS); ease_x/ease_y = fitted summary (no anticipation)

push._note: 7 frames after the last word: the grid hard-cuts off and the text + box push in (uniform scale about the text's ink centre): s(t) = 1 + A*ease(t/T) + k*t. Handle tables: [t from push, dx_U, dy_U] relative to the SCALED rect corner (corner scaled about the ink centre).
push._hold_note: Jake 2026-10-10: keep the push-in running 1 s longer at the same pace -> hold_s = measured 1.0 s (f30-f89) + 1.0 s; beyond the 60 measured frames the scale continues linearly at k_per_s (0.084/s). With wipe off (default) 'out' = the hard cut = push + hold_s.

out._note: beat 'out' = the dock rail starts fading in at the right frame edge; the handles then fly (ease-in, accelerate) into the rail's tab, each landing as a spinner ring; hard cut to the next shot 0.628 s after 'out'

tagline_build.exit: wipe off (default): hard cut at push + hold_s (beat 'out'); wipe on: hard cut at out + cut_after_out_s

defaults._note: Jake 2026-10-10 review: remove the dots and the right black bar; the measured dot/rail motion is kept in this file for the optional params

verb_swap._doc: verb_swap MEASURED motion (motion1.mp4, 30 fps, frame 1 = t 0). Design-free: times in s relative to the beat named in 'rel', travel in em of the line's font size, easings = fitted cubic-bezier [x1,y1,x2,y2] (max error in brackets). Words POP (opacity 0->1 in one frame, no blur, no scale); motion is horizontal only.

drift._doc: whole line slides LEFT into place while it builds (all words share it). offset(t) = dx_em*(1-E((t-in-start)/dur)); 81 px at the first frame, 0 by +0.70 s. [max err 0.20 px]

word_in._doc: each prefix word after the first pops in already slightly right of its slot and settles (on top of drift). Measured 3.7 / 5.0 / 8.9 px for Bot / can / now; mean used. [max err 0.47 px]

verb_in._doc: verb_0 and the suffix pop in together on beat verb_0, right of their slots, and slide left into place; the suffix travels ~1.6x the verb. Prefix does not move (the line is laid out for verb_0 from the first frame). [max err 1.35 px]

swap._doc: verb i-1 -> verb i: every word's x interpolates from the line laid out (centred) with verb i-1 to the line laid out with verb i; the verb is drawn centred in its interpolated slot. Motion starts lead_s BEFORE the beat; the verb TEXT and colour switch hard ON the beat (no roll, no fade, no blur). The line therefore re-centres with the width change. Default = one bezier fitted to both reference swaps (per-swap timing) [max err 0.056 progress]; measured[i-1] is used for swap i when present.
swap._min_gap_doc: overlap guard for generalisation: during a swap the prefix/suffix are pushed apart so the displayed verb's advance box never comes closer than min_gap_em to its neighbours (reference minimum ~ -0.03 em at the swap frames, so the guard never alters the reference replica)

out._doc: the reference has NO exit (holds the full line to the clip end, 1.07 s after the last verb). On 'out' (or at duration) the line hard-cuts off, the reference's own pop vocabulary.

timing_defaults._doc: fallbacks when a beat is missing, from the reference spacing (s)
